meta.title: Solyx
meta.description: A desktop app for trading Taiwan and US stocks. An agent analyzes the market and proposes trades; nothing reaches your broker unless you confirm it or it falls within a mandate you set.

banner.app: Solyx is still in development. Builds are nightly and trade on a paper account.
banner.docs: These docs are still being written, so some of what Solyx does is not covered yet.

hero.lede: Solyx is a desktop app for trading Taiwan and US stocks. An agent reads the market and proposes orders, and nothing reaches your broker unless you confirm it or it falls within a mandate you set.
hero.note: Free and open source. Nightly builds trade on a paper account.

demo.title: Take a proposal from pencil to ink
demo.lede: This workspace runs in your browser on made-up prices. Pick a listing, ask the agent, and confirm its order yourself.
demo.no-proposals: Nothing waits for you. Proposals the agent drafts show up here.
demo.composer: The demo answers the questions above

ask.forecast: Where could {{code}} close in ten sessions?
ask.proposal: Draft a buy of one lot of {{code}} near support

reply.forecast: {{code}} closed at {{last}}, between the month's low at {{support}} and the fortnight's high at {{resistance}}. I put most weight on it staying in that range; history lands there a little less often.
reply.at-support: I drafted a limit buy at the month's low, {{limit}}. It passed the risk checks; MAGI carried it two to one. It waits for you.
reply.at-limit: The month's low, {{support}}, is below the next session's limit, so I drafted a limit buy at {{limit}}. It passed the risk checks; MAGI carried it two to one. It waits for you.

proposal.title: Order proposal
proposal.check-limits: Inside the next session's limits, {{low}} to {{high}}
proposal.submitted: The checks passed again, and the order went to the paper account.

magi.dip: A limit below the close fills only on a dip.
magi.paper: One lot on paper puts no real money at risk.
magi.flows: Foreign investors sold five sessions running.

legend.pencil-body: Hatching and dashed outlines mark what is not real yet: a proposal waiting for you, a forecast, the paper account. Nothing drawn in pencil has reached a broker.
legend.ink-body: An order turns to ink once you confirm it. Confirm is the only button Solyx fills with ink, and no setting lets the agent press it.

road.title: One road to an order
road.lede: Every order takes these five steps. No setting, mode or extension adds another way to the broker.

propose.title: The agent proposes
propose.detail: Its tools can draft a proposal and nothing more.

check.title: Risk checks run
check.detail: Lot size, tick, the day's limits, cash and the session.

confirm.title: You confirm
confirm.detail: Only your click in the app gets past this step.

recheck.title: The checks run again
recheck.detail: The market may have moved since the draft.

broker.title: The broker gets the order
broker.detail: A paper account until you switch a live broker on.

road.failed: A failed submission is never retried, since the broker may have taken the order anyway. Solyx marks it failed and leaves the next move to you.

sources.title: Runs on your keys
sources.lede: Market data and a model are enough to start. Every key is saved encrypted on your computer, and data flows straight between each provider and you, with no Solyx server between.
sources.more: Decisions models and embedders add more.

uses.quotes: Quotes, daily and intraday candles, and a live stream of one-minute bars.
uses.sectors: Taiwan's sector indices, from the same provider.

notes.fugle: Fugle takes an API key and your plan. Basic allows 60 intraday requests a minute and 5 streamed listings, Developer 600 and 300, Advanced 2,000 and 2,000.
notes.fubon: For Fubon, download its fubon-neo SDK yourself and point Solyx at the folder, then sign in with your ID number, a Fubon API key and the certificate you export from Fubon's site. The SDK never ships with Solyx.
notes.sign-in: A failed Fubon sign-in is not tried again on its own, since repeated failures can lock the account.
notes.cache: Closed sessions are cached on your computer, so a chart never downloads them twice.

uses.statements: Income statements, balance sheets, cash flows, monthly revenue and dividends.
uses.listing: Each listing's institutional buying and selling, margin and short balances, and foreign holdings.
uses.market: The market's institutional and margin totals, futures positions and trading calendar.

notes.limit: Without a token you get 300 requests an hour. A free token raises it to 600, and FinMind's paid plans go further.
notes.cache: A listing's fundamentals are kept for half a day, and its flows until FinMind's next update at 15:00, 18:00 or 21:00 Taipei time.

exchanges.purpose: Exchange lists, filings and insider transfers

uses.filings: Material information and the insider share transfers declared in advance.
uses.restrictions: Trading restrictions: short-sale and day-trading suspensions, disposition lists and halts.
uses.lists: The exchanges' P/E and other multiples, ex-dividend notices, shareholders' meetings and each company's industry.
uses.funds: TWSE's list of listed funds and the year's market closures.

notes.feeds: One request per list, never a crawl. Each list holds only its latest day, so Solyx builds the history as it collects.
notes.open-data: Only what the exchanges publish as open data is read, since TWSE's own sites forbid programs from downloading theirs.

uses.calendar: The release calendar for the next twelve months: CPI, GDP, the economic forecast, trade, industrial production, export orders, the business signal and PMI.
uses.figures: The figures for CPI, advance GDP, trade, export orders, industrial production and the business signal.

notes.schedule: The calendar is read at most twice a day, and the figures, covering the last 26 months, at most once an hour.
notes.session: The portal is read in a private session that keeps no cookies.

model.source: A model provider of your choice

uses.runs: Every reply and tool call the agent makes, on the model you pick for all conversations or for one.

notes.pay: Pay per request with an API key, or sign in to a plan you already have: ChatGPT for OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, SuperGrok or X Premium for xAI, and Muse for Meta.
notes.openrouter: OpenRouter's sign-in creates a key that is yours. Ollama runs models on your own computer and needs no key.
notes.gateway: You can send a provider's requests to your own gateway; a sign-in only ever goes to the provider itself.
notes.keychain: Keys and sign-ins are encrypted with your system's keychain, and a backup never holds them.

uses.search: The agent's web searches and the pages it reads.
uses.news: News on the listings you hold and watch: outlets' articles, and posts from Threads for Taiwan and X for the US.

notes.vendor: Pick one vendor. Firecrawl searches Google, while Exa and Tavily search their own indexes.
notes.approval: A search runs on its own. Reading a page asks you first, unless the page came from the conversation's own search.
notes.schedule: News is collected every three days by default, so a free tier covers about ten listings. Without a key, filings, insider transfers and PTT's Stock board still come in.

closing.title: Start on a paper account
closing.lede: Solyx is free and open source. It trades on paper until you switch a live broker on yourself.

download.title: Download Solyx
download.lede: Free and open source, for Macs with Apple silicon and 64-bit Windows.
download.elsewhere: Solyx runs on macOS and Windows. Open this page on your computer to download it.

nightly.name: Solyx Nightly
nightly.lede: Built from the newest commit that passed its checks, at most once every six hours. It installs beside Solyx and keeps its own data, settings and keys.

coming-soon.title: Coming soon
coming-soon.lede: Solyx has no stable release yet. Until then, Solyx Nightly is the one to try; it trades on a paper account.

download.first-launch: Neither installer is signed by a paid certificate yet, so your system warns you before the first launch.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.lede: What changed in each release, from the pull requests merged into it.
